Package main

Class ClusteringByInsway

java.lang.Object
main.ClusteringByInsway
public class ClusteringByInsway extends Object
In this preview version, input can be either

• Directed graph D with edge weights, supplied as multiple lines of form (String source, String target, Double weight), or

• Undirected edge-weighted graph U in this format.

Step I: extract the 2-core of U, or of the undirected form of D, as appropriate. After that, every object has total degree at least two in either case, and therefore participates in at least one "voter triangle" {xy, yz, yz}.

Step II: given an integer parameter K ≥ 2 (supplied at run time), scan the neighbors (case U) or out-neighbors (case D) of each object x, and retain edges only for the K nearest according to x's ranking (or d nearest, if x has d < K neighbors in case U or out-neighbors in case D). Call this set Gamma(x). Even in the case of input U, we save results as a DIRECTED weighted graph (S, A, w), because y in Gamma(x) does not imply x in Gamma(y). The weight function w is the same as the one we started with. As explained in the paper

• Rank-based linkage I: triplet comparisons and oriented simplicial complexes, Darling, Grilliette and Logan, 2022

this data supplies an orientation of the line graph of an undirected K-nearest neighbor graph on a set S of n objects.

The present JAVA API creates the edge-weighted linkage graph (S, B, sigma). Here B consists of pairs of mutual friends, and sigma is the in-sway. As t varies, the graph components for edges with in-sway at least t supplies a partition of S. This is rank-based linkage hierarchical clustering. The critical value of t is the smallest t such that the number of links whose in-sway exceeds t is less than the number of objects. The subcritical clustering uses links whose in-sway exceeds the critical value.

Three output files:

• CSV file for the linkage graph, whose lines are of form (String source, String target, int in-sway)

• CSV file indicating the component of the subcritical linkage graph to which each object belongs. Lines are of form (String object, int index), where the index points to a component of the subcritical linkage graph. Lines are lexicographically ordered by object.

• CSV file listing the objects in each numbered component of the subcritical linkage graph. Lines are of form (int index, {String object1, String object2, ...}) where {...} contains the objects in the component associated with the index. Lines are ordered by index. Hence an object in component j appears in the line indexed by j, and in no other line.

R. W. R. Darling
